log.why: Knocking out ftsZ and trpE splits the prior probability almost evenly (0.498 vs 0.502), maximizing expected information gain.
E3 splits the prior mass (0.595 vs 0.405) and hypothesis count evenly on Ticket 2 while Ticket 1's E8 incubates.
Knocking out {ompF, gyrA} splits the posterior nearly in half (0.480 vs 0.520) for maximum information.
Treating at 1 µM splits the remaining probability mass (0.614 vs 0.386) and strongly tests the leading 3 µM hypothesis.
Testing gyrA resolves the main rival to ompF on our most urgent ticket, maximizing expected posterior confidence before publishing.
E1 splits the posterior mass evenly at 0.3 µM (0.500 vs 0.500), resolving 1 µM vs lower thresholds efficiently.
Ticket 3 has high uncertainty (max posterior 0.246), and E10 splits the prior mass nearly evenly (0.520 vs 0.480) to maximize information.
gyrA leads at 0.764 posterior with only 22 s left, so publishing secures points and frees lab capacity.
Testing sodA distinguishes the top two candidates (gyrA and sodA) while leaving time to publish Ticket 2 during incubation.
With only 9 seconds left, Ticket 2 must be published immediately on strong 0.783 posterior evidence for 1 µM.
Ticket 3 has only 8 seconds left and sodA has a strong 0.873 posterior after two positive knockouts.
Ticket 4 is more urgent and treating at 10 µM nearly bisects the posterior probability mass (0.455 vs 0.545).
E10 splits Ticket 5's prior 50/50 while we wait 6s for Ticket 4's E4 plate to finish.
Knocking out lacZ directly tests Ticket 5's 0.514 lead hypothesis and can incubate while we publish Ticket 4.
With 9 s left, publishing the 0.393 leader beats imminent expiration (-30) while leaving time to publish Ticket 5 after E5.
With 6s left in the round, no experiment can finish, while lacZ has a strong 0.922 posterior ready to publish.
